questions.title: What standard of review does the 10th Circuit apply to a BIA’s denial of asylum under 8 U.S.C. § 1252?
questions.question_body: In Jimenez v. Bondi the court reviewed the BIA’s denial of asylum and stated that the review is limited to the "administrative record on which the order of removal is based" (citing § 1252(b)(4)(A)). The court also notes that the BIA’s findings are subject to the "substantial‑evidence" standard. I am confused about how the appellate court treats the IJ’s explanation of the same facts, whether it gives the conclusion de‑novo, and whether the review is "pre‑ponderance of the evidence" or something else. What exactly is the standard the appellate court uses, and how does it treat the record of the IJ versus the BIA?

questions.title: Can threats alone be considered past persecution under the INA?
questions.question_body: In Jimenez v. Bondi the court held that threats are not sufficient on their own unless accompanied by actual physical harm, citing Karki v. Holder, Chhetri v. Rosen, and others. I would like to understand what qualifies as "persecution" under § 1101(a)(42)(A) and whether psychological or emotional harm can substitute for physical harm. Also, are there statutory criteria that differentiate mere threats from persecution? Please clarify the standards and provide examples.

questions.title: How is the ‘central reason’ test applied to political opinion claims under asylum law?
questions.question_body: The court referenced Rivera‑Barrientos and Dallakoti, stating that the political opinion must be "at least one central reason" for the persecution, not incidental or subordinate. In Jimenez v. Bondi the court found the threats were primarily due to Jimenez’s involvement with Don Rafa, not his political opinion. Could you explain how a court determines the centrality of political opinion, what evidence is needed to prove it, and how courts treat cases with "mixed motives"?

questions.title: How significant is a single police officer’s statement in the government‑protection assessment for asylum?
questions.question_body: In the case, the plaintiffs only spoke to a lone police officer who told them not to seek trouble, and the court said this is not enough to show that the Colombian government was unwilling or unable to protect them. I want to understand how the "notice" and "reporting" requirement is applied and how much weight a single officer’s attitude carries. Could you explain the guidelines or precedent for evaluating such evidence?

questions.title: What standard governs determining if an applicant can safely relocate within their country?
questions.question_body: Jimenez v. Bondi says the applicant must show that they could mitigate the threat by internal relocation based on a preponderance of the evidence, citing Rivera‑Barrientos. I’m confused about the evidence required: Does the applicant need to produce a relocation plan, proof of safe areas, or simply that family resides safely? How does the court evaluate "reasonable" relocation?

questions.title: How does the legal definition of 'refugee' under 8 U.S.C. § 1101(a)(42)(A) interact with the requirement of a well‑founded fear of future persecution?
questions.question_body: In the opinion, the Court said asylum requires proof of either past persecution or a well‑founded fear of future persecution, but "well‑founded fear" applies in the withholding context too. I’m uncertain how the statutory definition and the standard of proof differ between asylum and withholding, especially with reference to the threshold evidence required for each. Please explain the relationship.

questions.title: Do asylum applicants need to invoke the 'particular social group' ground if they are claiming political opinion?
questions.question_body: Jimenez v. Bondi notes that the plaintiffs did not brief a particular social group; they only alleged persecution for political opinion. I’m confused whether it’s possible to argue asylum denial under the political opinion ground without also addressing the particular social group requirement. Is it necessary to include the particular social group argument if the applicant only believes that the government is targeting them on political grounds? Clarify.
